question.text: Given that $y=3\ln x +2e^x$, find the slope of the tangent at $x=1.$
question.explanation:
To find the slope of the tangent at a given point, we have to find $\dfrac {\textrm{d}y} {\textrm{d}x}$ at that point.

Taking the derivative, we have

\[ \dfrac{\textrm{d}y}{\textrm{d}x}=\dfrac{3}{x}+2e^x \,. \]

Therefore, the slope of the tangent at $x=1$ is \[ \eqalign{ \left.\dfrac {\textrm{d}y} {\textrm{d}x}\right|_{x=1} &=\left.\left(\dfrac{3}{x}+2e^x \right)\right|_{x=1}\\[5pt] &=\dfrac{3}{1}+2e^1\\[5pt] &=3+2e \,. } \]

question.text: Given the function $y=-3\ln x+4e^x,$ the slope of the tangent line at $x=1$ is
question.explanation:
To find the slope of the tangent at a given point, we have to find $\dfrac {\textrm{d}y}{\textrm{d}x}$ at that point.

Taking the derivative, we have \[ \eqalign{ \dfrac{\textrm{d}y}{\textrm{d}x} &=\dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}\left(-3\ln x+4e^x\right)\\[5pt] &=-3\dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}\left(\ln x\right)+4\dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}\left(e^x\right)\\[5pt] &=-3\cdot\dfrac{1}{x}+4e^x\\[5pt] &=-\dfrac{3}{x}+4e^x \,. } \]

Therefore, the slope of the tangent at $x=1$ is \[ \eqalign{ \left.\dfrac {\textrm{d}y}{\textrm{d}x}\right|_{x=1} &=\left.\left(-\dfrac{3}{x}+4e^x\right)\right|_{x=1}\\[5pt] &=-\dfrac{3}{1}+4e^1\\[5pt] &= \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{-3+4e} \,. } \]

example.title: Calculating the Slope of the Tangent Line of a Logarithmic Function at a Point
